expected.title: Liberty Triumphant: Or the Downfall of Oppression

title_translations.es: La libertad triunfante: o la caída de la opresión

expected.credit_line: Gift of Mrs. J. Percy Sabin

traps.confusable_separator: Vision reads the accession as '38.447•4' — the third separator is U+2022 BULLET, not U+002E. Confidence 1.00, no clipping. This is THE regression case: the primary key is silently corrupted and neither confidence nor geometry catches it. See D14.
traps.two_years_on_one_line: 'Gift of Mrs. J. Percy Sabin, 1938. (38.447.4)' contains the donation year 1938 AND an accession beginning 38. A parser hunting for year-like numbers can easily take 1938 as the accession, or read '1938.' as its first component.
traps.attribution_is_not_authorship: 'Attributed to' must survive as a qualifier. Flattening it to created_by asserts something the museum explicitly declines to assert (§4.6).
traps.bilingual_duplication: Title and essay each appear twice, English then Spanish. An extractor taking 'the first two lines' as the title gets the English; one taking 'all lines before the date' gets both languages concatenated. Neither is right without language detection.
traps.circa: 'ca. 1774' is EDTF 1774~. Storing 1774 loses the approximation (D5).

work_photo_note: The engraving itself is dense with text — an engraved title, place names, speech banderoles, and a numbered key. OCR of the WORK photo returned 41 lines, mostly garbage against 18th-century engraved script ('LIBERI \"RIUMPIAN I;orthe Downfall of OPPRESSION.'). See D15: line count cannot distinguish a work photo from a label photo.
